newsitem.title: UK: London gold lethargic, pins hopes on silver.
newsitem.headline: London gold lethargic, pins hopes on silver.

text.p: The gold market, apathetic and floundering for direction, nevertheless perked up on Wednesday after silver started ticking a bit higher, dealers said.
"No one's making a decision on gold at all," one said. "Dealers are pushing bits and pieces between each other with a little bit of producer selling and physical buying."
However, gold was likely to mimic any moves by silver, the recent leader of the precious metals, dealers said.
Bullion fixed firmer at $381.50 an ounce, compared to $380.80 in the morning and $381.00 on Tuesday afternoon.
But to get the market rolling higher or lower, prices needed to move to the fringes of the broader $378-$384 price range.
"At the $381-$382 area no one's interested," a dealer said, referring to the current lack of investor and speculative interest in the gold market.
U.S. consumer price figures, up 0.3 percent in line with expectations, had no effect on gold prices.
The fear of inflation traditionally boosts gold's allure to investors, but analysts said the U.S. figures were benign.
Silver pushed a bit higher and was indicated at $5.05/$5.07 an ounce, up three cents from Tuesday's London close. But it faced tough resistance around $5.10.
"I don't think there's strong interest, it's just a speculative play to get it higher and then wallop it down," a dealer said, adding that heavy selling was also expected between $5.15 and $5.20.
But dealers said the weakness of platinum and palladium, which were drifting lower due to oversupply and slack demand, were helping depress silver prices.
"While the platinum group metals are under pressure that stops silver rallying," a dealer said.
Palladium remained bearish after slipping to fresh three year lows on Tuesday, burdened by oversupply from Russian producers and low consumer demand.
It was unchanged at $116.00/$117, although dealers said it could easily drop further.
"I couldn't even give you a floor," one dealer said. "When ther is just no supporting factor it could go where it likes."
Platinum came off the day's lows, but was still off $0.25 from Tuesday's London close at $384.75/$385.75 an ounce.
Dealers said it was vulnerable towards recent lows around the $380 support level.
